content: Examples of drugs that may be affected by this medication include atazanavir, dasatinib, certain azole antifungals (such as itraconazole and ketoconazole), levoketoconazole, pazopanib, and sparsentan, among others. Cigarette smoking can also influence the effectiveness of this medication. This medication, along with other H2 blockers like famotidine, nizatidine, and ranitidine, is available both with and without a prescription. In the event of an overdose, if the individual exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, immediately call emergency services (911). Otherwise, contact a poison control center without delay. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, while Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Lifestyle modifications, such as engaging in stress reduction programs, quitting smoking, limiting alcohol consumption, and making dietary changes (e.g., avoiding caffeine and spicy foods), may enhance the effectiveness of this medication. Regular laboratory and/or medical tests may be required during the course of treatment. It is essential to attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Avoid storing it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly dispose of this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information was last revised in June 2024. It is important to note that this summary does not contain all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individualized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Cimetidine is used to treat ulcers in the stomach and intestines and to prevent their recurrence after healing. It is also used to manage certain stomach and esophageal conditions caused by excessive stomach acid, such as Zollinger-Ellison syndrome, erosive esophagitis, and acid reflux disease (GERD). By reducing excess stomach acid, this medication can alleviate symptoms such as stomach pain, heartburn, difficulty swallowing, coughing, and sleep disturbances. Cimetidine belongs to a class of drugs known as H2 blockers. It is also available over the counter for the treatment of occasional heartburn caused by excess stomach acid (acid indigestion or sour stomach) and for the prevention of heartburn and acid indigestion triggered by specific foods and beverages. If using this medication for self-treatment, carefully read the manufacturer's package instructions to understand when to seek medical advice. If using the liquid form of this medication, measure the dose accurately with a special measuring device or spoon. The dosage and duration of treatment depend on your medical condition and response to therapy. Follow your doctor’s instructions precisely. Take this medication regularly as prescribed to achieve the maximum benefit. To help you remember, take it at the same time(s) each day. Do not increase your dose or take it more frequently than directed. Continue taking this medication for the prescribed duration, even if you feel better. For self-treatment of acid indigestion or heartburn with nonprescription cimetidine, take one tablet orally with a glass of water as needed. To prevent heartburn, take one tablet orally with a glass of water right before or up to 30 minutes before consuming food or beverages that cause heartburn. Do not take more than two tablets in 24 hours unless directed by your doctor. Common side effects of this medication include headache, dizziness, drowsiness, or diarrhea. If your doctor has prescribed this medication, remember that they have determined the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Before taking cimetidine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to other H2 blockers (such as famotidine, nizatidine, or ranitidine), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. Some symptoms may indicate a more serious condition. Liquid formulations may contain sugar and/or alcohol, so caution is advised if you have diabetes, liver disease, or any condition requiring dietary restrictions. This drug may cause dizziness or drowsiness. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate these effects. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks requiring alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. Older adults may be more sensitive to the side effects of this drug, particularly confusion and lung infections (pneumonia). During pregnancy, cimetidine should only be used when clearly necessary. This medication passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter the way your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all the products you use (including prescription/nonprescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Cimetidine can slow the elimination of other medications from your body, potentially affecting their efficacy. Additionally, by reducing stomach acid, cimetidine may alter the absorption of certain medications, impacting their effectiveness. Examples of affected drugs include atazanavir, dasatinib, certain azole antifungals (such as itraconazole and ketoconazole), levoketoconazole, pazopanib, and sparsentan. Cigarette smoking may also influence the effectiveness of this medication.
